description:
Give gate keys one validated type in gate definitions, gate-run results, gate events and the storage trait.

## Background

`GateDefinition.key` is a `String` (`crates/jit/src/declarations/gates.rs:159`), and the registry enforces no grammar on it; loading checks only duplicates (`gates.rs:281`). `GateRunResult.gate_key` (`domain/types.rs:943`) and the gate event variants (`types.rs:1339,1352,1365,1376`) hold strings, as do `IssueStore::find_reusable_gate_run(gate_key: &str, ..)` (`storage/mod.rs:287-289`) and `GateRunResult::is_reusable_for` (`types.rs:1022`). Each gate key in this repository is lowercase-kebab. The domain's lowercase-kebab predicate, shared with profile ids, lives in `domain::identity`.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: `domain::identity::GateKey` accepts keys that satisfy the shared lowercase-kebab predicate and rejects other input with an error naming the key.
- [hard] REQ-02: A gate registry holding a malformed key fails to load with that error, and defining a gate with a malformed key is rejected.
- [hard] REQ-03: `GateDefinition.key`, `GateRunResult.gate_key`, the gate fields of event bodies and `find_reusable_gate_run` use `GateKey`.
- [hard] REQ-04: The gate registry of this repository parses with its declarations equal after a serialize-and-parse round trip, and re-serializing that output is byte-identical. Current-format gate-run records and the event log of this repository load and re-serialize byte-identically, and every other stored gate-run record decodes and reproduces its id fields.

## Notes

The grammar is the engine's own token rule, so it is mechanism rather than repository vocabulary (`@/inv/domain-agnostic`).
title: Gate keys are a validated GateKey in the registry and gate runs
